notes: Access: direct HTTP fetch, no proxy needed (consistent with prior Furniture-pass notes for SR32). robots.txt checked first: no Claude-specific full-site Disallow (ClaudeBot has only Crawl-delay:1); a generic wildcard rule disallows /search/ for crawling but that only governs bot crawling, not this direct-fetch access. Checked: homepage full HTML (mega-menu flyout tiles per department, e.g. Art flyout shows only 'New Arrivals' and 'Sale' promo tiles, no Bestsellers/Popular/Trending tile), footer links, the site's own /sitemap/ index page, robots.txt (which disallows a '/*topSeller=*' query param - this reads as an internal facet/tracking parameter, not a public browsable Bestsellers page, and it is not linked from any nav/footer/sitemap so it was not treated as a candidate PLP). Direct URL probes all 404: /best-sellers/, /bestsellers/. Site search (https://www.1stdibs.com/search/?q=...) for 'best-sellers', 'bestsellers', 'popular', 'trending' all return non-zero counts but every one has the generic homepage fallback og:title '1stDibs: Antique and Modern Furniture, Jewelry, Fashion & Art' - i.e. these are plain full-text keyword search-results pages (the word appearing somewhere in listing titles/descriptions), not dedicated merchandising PLPs, so excluded per the search-results-pages exclusion. The homepage has a 'Now Trending' module but its GraphQL type is explicitly 'EditorialModule'/type:'editorial' with individual curated items, not a real product-listing PLP with its own count - excluded as editorial content per brief. No local-language check needed (site_url is the USA/English 1stdibs.com property). Conclusion: no genuine Bestsellers-equivalent merchandising PLP exists on this property.
